name: Raptor 3 (sea-level variant)
_status: partial: thrustVac_kN and ispSL_s TODO(source). Not usable by physics.js until both are filled (see _candidates).

thrustSL_kN.quote: Raptor 3 engines deliver increased thrust, with sea-level variants now producing 250 tf (551,000 lbf) up from 230 tf (507,000 lbf), while vacuum engines produce 275 tf (606,000 lbf) up from 258 tf (568,000 lbf).
thrustSL_kN.quote2: {label:"Thrust",value:"250 tf",secondValue:" / 551 klbf"} (Raptor tile, spacex.com/vehicles/starship, served from https://www.spacex.com/2337.c79c2132bc6aff75.js)
thrustSL_kN.note: V3 flight rating (SpaceX update "Introducing Starship V3", 2026-05-12; CMS JSON https://content.spacex.com/api/spacex-website/updates, updateId starship-v3). SpaceX does not say whether 250 tf is measured at sea level; taken as the sea-level rating. SpaceX's 3 Aug 2024 post gave 280 tf for the same engine (https://x.com/SpaceX/status/1819772716339339664); the 2026 figure is used as the current official one.

ispVac_s.quote: Raptor 3 (sea level variant) Thrust: 280tf Specific impulse: 350s Engine mass: 1525kg Engine + vehicle-side commodities and hardware mass : 1720kg
ispVac_s.note: SpaceX post, 3 Aug 2024 (read through api.fxtwitter.com). SpaceX does not say sea level or vacuum. Mapped to VACUUM: SpaceX's matching figure for Raptor 2 is 347 s, while the FAA's 2022 plume report gives Raptor 2 about 316 s at sea level (see raptor-2 _candidates), so 347/350 s cannot be sea-level values. Wikipedia's engine table (oldid 1380574902) also lists 350 s in its vacuum column, citing the same post.

mass_kg.quote: Mass of the Raptor sea-level engines has been reduced to 1,525 kg from 1,630 kg.
mass_kg.note: Same figure in the 2024 post ("Engine mass: 1525kg"). Engine only; with vehicle-side hardware SpaceX gives 1,720 kg.

diameter_m.quote: {name:"Raptor",...metrics:[{label:"Diameter",value:"1.3 m",secondValue:" / 4.2 ft"},{label:"Height",value:"2.9 m",secondValue:" / 9.5 ft"},{label:"Thrust",value:"250 tf",secondValue:" / 551 klbf"}]
diameter_m.note: SpaceX does not say what Diameter measures. Consistent with the FAA's Raptor 2 nozzle exit (1.306 m, raptor-2). Height 2.9 m is a visuals.json fact (engine length), not a contract field.

thrustVac_kN.todo: TODO(source): SpaceX publishes no vacuum thrust for the sea-level Raptor.

ispSL_s.todo: TODO(source): no published sea-level Isp for Raptor 3. The FAA/Space Force plume appendices for Raptor 3 give emissions only (no total plume flow), so the Raptor 2 method below cannot be repeated.

thrustVac_kN.derived: (Starship tile thrust 1,614 tf − 3 × RVac 275 tf) / 3 = 263 tf = 2,579.1 kN. Assumes the Starship tile is the ship's total VACUUM thrust: at sea-level ratings 3 × 250 + 3 × 275 = 1,575 tf, not 1,614, while the Super Heavy tile (8,240 tf ≈ 33 × 250) is a sea-level sum.
thrustVac_kN.quote: {label:"Thrust",value:"1,614 tf",secondValue:" / 3.5 Mlbf"} (Starship tile); "Starship is powered by six engines, three Raptor engines, and three Raptor Vacuum (RVac) engines"

ispSL_s.derived: 350 s × 250 tf / 263 tf: same propellant flow at sea level and in vacuum (choked nozzle), so Isp scales with thrust. Rests on the thrustVac candidate above.

ispSL_s.todo: TODO(source): no published figure; a value derived from the FAA plume report is in _candidates

ispSL_s.derived: engine propellant flow = total mixed plume flow − entrained air = 432,386 − 430,783 = 1,603 lbm/s = 727.1 kg/s; Isp = 230 tf / 727.1 kg/s = 316.3 s. Cross-check: a carbon balance on the same report (CO2 1,202.5 lbm/s minus the CO2 of the entrained air, exit-plane CO2/CO/CH4 fractions in its Table 3) gives 1,589 lbm/s, within 1 %.
ispSL_s.quote: Integration of the SPF data indicates that 430,783 lbm/s air is entrained by the core jet
ispSL_s.quote2: Given the total mixed plume mass flow rate of 432,386 lb/s, this corresponds to 5.62 lbm/s for NO and 2.59 lbm/s CO.
ispSL_s.confidence: derived from an FAA document (model matched to test data: "model results matched test performance data") and SpaceX's 230 tf; assumes the report ran at the 230 tf rating (it says only "100% nominal engine operating condition").
